description: RC thermal model for pseudocapacitor (e.g. RuO2 or MnO2). Extends F1a with Arrhenius ESR(T), temperature-dependent capacitance, leakage current, and heat generation. Pseudocapacitance from faradaic surface reactions adds a battery-like entropic heat term absent in EDLC.

cell.name: Generic RuO2 pseudocapacitor cell, 1 V class
cell.source: Conway, B. E. (1999). Electrochemical Supercapacitors. Kluwer/Plenum; Trasatti, S., Buzzanca, G. (1971). J. Electroanal. Chem. 29, A1; Zheng, J. P. et al. (1995). J. Electrochem. Soc. 142, 2699

capacitance_ref.note: Pseudocapacitance at T_ref (298.15 K). RuO2 cells: 100-1000 F depending on mass loading; 200 F typical for small module.

esr_ref.note: ESR at T_ref; pseudocapacitors have slightly higher ESR than EDLC due to charge-transfer resistance at electrode-electrolyte interface (~5 mOhm typical)

v_max.note: Rated voltage for RuO2 in H2SO4 electrolyte (voltage window ~1 V; MnO2 in neutral electrolyte also ~1 V)

leakage_resistance.note: Self-discharge resistance; pseudocapacitors have higher leakage than EDLC due to faradaic side reactions and parasitic redox. Ref: Simon & Gogotsi (2008) Nature Materials 7, 845.

E_a_esr.note: Activation energy for ESR in pseudocapacitor. Higher than EDLC (8 kJ/mol) due to faradaic charge-transfer activation energy at RuO2 surface. Literature values: 10-15 kJ/mol.
E_a_esr.source: Sugimoto, W. et al. (2006). Electrochim. Acta 52, 1742; Zheng et al. (1995) J. Electrochem. Soc. 142, 2699

alpha_C.note: Capacitance temperature coefficient; pseudocapacitance increases with T due to improved ion/proton kinetics at electrode surface. ~0.4%/K, slightly higher than EDLC due to activated surface reactions.
alpha_C.source: Conway (1999); Sugimoto et al. (2006) Electrochim. Acta 52, 1742

dOCV_dT_specific.note: Entropic coefficient for pseudocapacitor charge-transfer reactions. RuO2 proton insertion: RuO2 + H+ + e- -> RuO(OH). dE0/dT for proton insertion ~ -0.2 mV/K (smaller than full battery reactions). Contributes to reversible heat.

temperature.note: -30 to 60 degC; narrower than EDLC due to aqueous electrolyte constraints
